subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what the city is actually doing, minute by minute.

subsystems.name: Connectivity and edge compute
subsystems.role: moves that data cheaply and processes it near where it is generated.
parts: public cellular and low-power wide-area networks
edge servers in substations and cabinets

subsystems.name: Urban digital twin
subsystems.role: a live 3-D model of buildings, roads, pipes and people that can be simulated forward.

subsystems.name: Control and actuation
subsystems.role: the part that actually changes the city's behaviour.
parts: street lighting and building HVAC controls

subsystems.name: Data governance layer
subsystems.role: decides who may see, combine and act on which data.

subsystems.name: Operations centre and interfaces
subsystems.role: where humans supervise the loop and where residents can see and challenge it.

buildSteps.title: Inventory assets and data
buildSteps.detail: Survey what the city owns, what sensors exist, who holds each dataset and how fresh it is.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the gaps
buildSteps.detail: Add counting, air-quality and flow sensors where coverage is missing, favouring cheap devices in large numbers over a few expensive ones.

buildSteps.title: Standardise the data
buildSteps.detail: Force every feed into shared schemas and open interfaces so systems from different vendors can be combined.

buildSteps.title: Build the static twin
buildSteps.detail: Assemble 3-D city geometry — much of it converted from building information models — into one coherent model.

buildSteps.title: Make it live
buildSteps.detail: Stream sensor and transit data into the model so it reflects the city now, not last year.

buildSteps.title: Add simulation
buildSteps.detail: Model traffic, energy, water and pedestrian flow so the twin can predict the effect of a change before it is made.

buildSteps.title: Close the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect forecasts to actuators — signals, setpoints, dispatch — first with a human approving every action, later within bounded rules.

buildSteps.title: Set the governance
buildSteps.detail: Agree what is collected, how long it is kept, who can combine it, and publish the rules.

buildSteps.title: Operate and retrain
buildSteps.detail: Run continuously, measure outcomes against the baseline, and correct the models when they drift.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap, networked environmental and flow sensors
prerequisites.why: the twin is only as good as the density and reliability of its measurements.
standards such as CityGML and IFC exist and city models such as Virtual Singapore have been built, but few cities hold complete, current geometry.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time edge compute and low-latency networks
prerequisites.why: traffic and energy control must respond in seconds without shipping all data to a distant cloud.
traffic and energy models work separately; coupling them across a whole city is largely unproven.
most urban equipment is locked to a single vendor's protocol, so one system cannot safely command another.
continuous sensing of public space is legally and socially contested in most democracies.

pathway.milestone: siloed smart systems: adaptive signals, smart meters, building management
shared city data platforms and 3-D twins fed by live feeds
coupled simulation across transport, energy and water
pathway.unlocks: decisions assessed for side-effects before implementation.

pathway.milestone: bounded closed-loop control with human override
pathway.unlocks: signals, setpoints and dispatch optimised continuously city-wide.

pathway.milestone: self-optimising city responding to real-time human need
pathway.unlocks: the 'single organism' vision — achievable only if governance and interoperability problems are solved first, and it may prove neither desirable nor safe.
